mainTopic: Immersing to eat תרומת חוץ לארץ, and the sources for a בכור's birth-year and its two-days-one-night eating limit
overview: This amud opens with a question about a טמא מת: can he immerse and eat תרומה grown in חוץ לארץ, when we have no הזאה? רב עמרם arrives and quotes רב, who says yes. The גמרא rules that the הלכה is not like רב, and it adds a similar lenient view of רב ששת about a טמא שרץ, which is also not the הלכה. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's rule that a בכור is eaten 'שנה בשנה'. From the word 'שנתו' it infers that the year is counted from the animal's birth. רב learns this from the פסוק 'שנה בשנה', meaning a year that runs into the next year. דבי רב instead read those words as teaching that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night. Each side then gets a different source for the other law. דבי רב learn the birth-year rule from 'כבש בן שנתו'. רב learns the two-days-one-night limit from a היקש to the חזה ושוק of שלמים.

steps.title: Challenge: we have no sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: Someone objects that immersion cannot help a טמא מת today, because there is no הזאה.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone attacks the claim that a טמא מת can immerse and eat תרומה from חוץ לארץ. The point is that we have no red heifer ashes to sprinkle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who becomes impure from a corpse needs הזאה on the third and seventh days, and only then does immersion work. Without פרה אדומה ashes, immersion alone seems useless. So how could he ever eat תרומה?

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinkling of water mixed with red heifer ashes, which purifies from corpse impurity
A person made impure by contact with a dead body
The priestly portion of produce, which may only be eaten in purity

steps.confusionAlert: Immersion (טבילה) alone does NOT remove טומאת מת. The sprinkling is also required. That is the whole force of this question.

phrases.english: But do we have sprinkling?
phrases.notes: Without the ashes of the פרה אדומה, a טמא מת cannot become fully pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the discussion earlier about immersing to eat תרומת חוץ לארץ.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a טמא מת may immerse and eat תרומת חוץ לארץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Corpse impurity requires הזאה, which is unavailable, so immersion alone should not help.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא: shouldn't we consider the old man's view?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא suggests the elder sage's tradition should be taken into account before the matter is decided.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said to him: Shouldn't we be concerned for the old man?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא steps in and suggests waiting to hear what the elder, רב עמרם, holds. This sets up the next move, when רב עמרם arrives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of settling the question by logic alone, רמי בר חמא points to the authority of an older sage who may hold a received tradition. The debate is now waiting on a teaching that has been passed down.

keyTerms.meaning: Shouldn't we be concerned / take into account?
The old man, an elder sage (here, רב עמרם)

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said to him:
Shouldn't we be concerned for the old man?
phrases.notes: Following Sefaria, this is a rhetorical question: we should consider the elder's opinion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge by pointing to the opinion of an elder authority.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the elder sage's tradition say about this case?

steps.title: רב עמרם arrives and quotes רב
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם arrives and reports that רב ruled a טמא מת may immerse and eat תרומת חוץ לארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, רב עמרם came. He said to them: This is what רב said: one impure from a corpse may immerse and eat תרומה from חוץ לארץ.
steps.whatsHappening: Just then רב עמרם arrives and gives a tradition in the name of רב. It permits a טמא מת to immerse and eat תרומה from חוץ לארץ, even without הזאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's ruling answers the challenge from Step 1. The likely reasoning is that תרומת חוץ לארץ is only a rabbinic obligation, so the חכמים were lenient and let immersion alone be enough, even for a טמא מת. So the missing הזאה does not block eating it.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile, at that moment
Immerses and eats
תרומה from produce grown outside ארץ ישראל (a rabbinic obligation)

phrases.english: Meanwhile, Rav Amram came.
He said to them: This is what Rav said:
One impure from a corpse immerses and eats
teruma from outside the Land.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּהָכִי אֲתָא רַב עַמְרָם, אֲמַר לְהוּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the tradition that רמי בר חמא wanted to hear.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב holds that a טמא מת may immerse and eat תרומת חוץ לארץ, even without הזאה.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that the הלכה is not like רב's lenient view.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the הלכה is not in accordance with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling: we do not follow רב's lenient tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's view is recorded as a real opinion, but it is rejected in practice. A טמא מת still may not eat תרומת חוץ לארץ just by immersing.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is not like him

phrases.english: But the halacha is not in accordance with him,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final halachic verdict on רב's ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A טמא מת may not rely on immersion alone to eat תרומת חוץ לארץ.

steps.title: רב ששת's parallel ruling about a שרץ
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא quotes רב ששת that even a טמא שרץ may immerse and eat תרומת חוץ לארץ, and that view too is not the הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As מר זוטרא said in the name of רב ששת: one impure from a creeping animal immerses and eats תרומה from חוץ לארץ. And the הלכה is not in accordance with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a similar lenient statement about a טמא שרץ. It notes that this one, too, is not followed in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טומאת שרץ is a lighter impurity that needs no הזאה. Yet even there the lenient ruling is rejected. So it is all the more clear that רב's leniency for the more severe טומאת מת is not followed.

keyTerms.meaning: A person made impure by touching a dead creeping creature
In the name of

steps.whatToRemember: Two lenient opinions (רב for a טמא מת, רב ששת for a טמא שרץ) allow immersing and eating תרומת חוץ לארץ. The הלכה follows neither of them.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: As Mar Zutra said in the name of Rav Sheshet:
One impure from a creeping animal immerses and eats
teruma from outside the Land,
and the halacha is not in accordance with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב שֵׁשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the rejection of רב by pointing to a parallel lenient view that is also rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה does not follow רב's leniency for a טמא מת
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב ששת's ruling about a טמא שרץ, which is also not the הלכה

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a בכור is eaten year by year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new section by quoting the משנה: a בכור is eaten שנה בשנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A firstborn is eaten year by year, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the next line of the משנה. This sets up the analysis that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that a בכור, blemished or unblemished, must be eaten within its first year. The גמרא will now examine exactly how that year is counted.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male kosher animal, given to the כהן
Year by year: within its first year

phrases.english: A firstborn is eaten year by year, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New section of the sugya, based on the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בכור must be eaten within its first year.

steps.title: Inference: the year is counted from the animal's birth
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's phrase 'within ITS year', the גמרא infers that the year is counted from the animal's birth, not by the calendar.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it says 'a blemish developed within its year,' this tells us that we count by its own year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the exact wording of the משנה closely. It concludes that each בכור has its own personal year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said 'שנתו' (its year), not just 'the year'. That word shows the year starts from the day the animal was born, not from ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that it says
That is to say / this implies
We count

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the בכור's year ends at ראש השנה. It is a full year counted from the animal's own birthday.

phrases.english: From the fact that it says 'a blemish developed in it within its year,'
that is to say that we count by its own year.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר נוֹלַד בּוֹ מוּם בְּתוֹךְ שְׁנָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a precise rule from the wording of the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The year of a בכור is counted from its birth.

steps.title: Asking for the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the בכור's year is counted from its birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a scriptural source for the rule it just inferred. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An inference from the משנה's wording is not enough on its own. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (derived)? A request for a source

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the inference made in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a בכור's year is counted from its birth.

steps.title: Derivation from 'שנה בשנה'
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב: 'שנה בשנה' means a year that runs into another year, and that is the בכור's own year.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יהודה said in the name of רב: the verse says, 'Before the Lord your God you shall eat it year by year.' Which year enters into another year? You must say: the year of the firstborn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. 'שנה בשנה' literally means 'a year in a year', and only the בכור's personal year fits that description.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A calendar year never overlaps another calendar year. A בכור born in the middle of the year has a first year that runs into the next calendar year. So the פסוק must mean the year is counted from the animal's birth.

keyTerms.meaning: As the verse says
That enters into its fellow (the next year)
You must say: introduces the only possible answer

steps.whatToRemember: A בכור must be eaten within twelve months of its birth. This comes from 'שנה בשנה', a year that overlaps into the next year.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the deadline for eating every בכור, and the same 'personal year' counting is used in other laws as well.

phrases.english: As Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav,
for the verse says:
'Before the Lord your God you shall eat it
year by year' (literally: a year in a year),
Which year enters into another year?
You must say: the year of the firstborn.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the פסוק requested in Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'שנה בשנה' refers to a year that overlaps into the next year, which can only be the בכור's personal year counted from its birth.

steps.title: The school of רב reads 'year by year' as two days and one night
steps.stepSummary: דבי רב teach that 'שנה בשנה' means one day in this year and one day in the next. This teaches that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב taught: 'Year by year' means one day in this year and one day in that year. This teaches that the בכור is eaten for two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second way to read the same words 'שנה בשנה' that רב just explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב used these words to teach that the year is counted from the animal's birth. דבי רב use them for a different law: picture a בכור slaughtered on the last day of the year. It may be eaten that day, the night after, and the next day, which is already the new year. So the words teach how long the meat may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: The school (study hall) of רב
'Year by year' — the verse's phrase about eating the בכור
Two days and one night — the time limit for eating the meat

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about the yearly deadline for bringing the בכור. It is about how long the meat may be eaten once it has been slaughtered. Here the 'two years' are really just two days that fall on either side of the change of year.

phrases.english: The school of Rav taught:
'Year by year' —
one day in this year,
and one day in that year,
it taught about the firstborn
that it is eaten for two days and one night.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same verse that רב explained in step 9
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'שנה בשנה' teaches that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night

steps.title: Where do the school of רב learn the birth-year rule?
steps.stepSummary: Since דבי רב used 'שנה בשנה' for the eating limit, the גמרא asks where they learn that the בכור's year is counted from its birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב — from where do they learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks דבי רב for their source for the rule that רב took from 'שנה בשנה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree to the birth-year rule. But דבי רב already 'used up' the verse on a different law. So they need another source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do they know it? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: The school of Rav — from where do they derive it?
phrases.notes: 'It' means the rule that the year is counted from birth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what follows from דבי רב's reading in step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: דבי רב's source for counting the בכור's year from its birth

steps.title: They learn it from other sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: דבי רב learn the birth-year rule from other קדשים, whose age is counted from birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from other sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that דבי רב compare the בכור to other קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With other קדשים, an animal's year is counted from when it was born. The בכור follows the same pattern. This answer will itself need a source, which the גמרא asks for next.

keyTerms.meaning: They learn (derive) it
Sacrifices; holy offerings

phrases.english: They derive it from other sacrifices,

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The בכור's year is learned from other קדשים, whose age is counted from birth

steps.title: Where do we know this about other sacrifices?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that the age of other קדשים is counted from birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the sacrifices themselves — from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes one step back and asks how we know the rule for קדשים in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Learning from קדשים only works if the rule for קדשים itself comes from the Torah. So the גמרא asks for that root source.

keyTerms.meaning: Themselves
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And the sacrifices themselves — from where do we derive it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the answer in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse showing that the age of קדשים is counted from birth

steps.title: 'A lamb in its year' means its own year
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב cites 'כבש בן שנתו': the word 'its year' means the animal's own year, not the calendar year.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: The verse says 'a lamb in its year' — its own year, and not the year of the world's count.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב gives the verse that is the root source for counting a קרבן's age from its birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse could have said 'a one-year-old lamb.' Instead it says 'its year.' That word 'its' ties the year to the animal itself. So the year starts on the animal's birthday, not on ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A lamb in its (first) year
The world's count — the calendar year

steps.whatToRemember: The age of קדשים, and so also of the בכור, is counted from the animal's birth because of the word 'שנתו' — its own year.

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Yaakov said:
The verse says 'a lamb in its year' —
its own year,
and not a year of the world's count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'כבש בן שנתו' — the year belongs to the animal, so it is counted from birth

steps.title: Where does רב learn the two-days-one-night rule?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא turns to רב: since he used 'שנה בשנה' for the birth-year rule, where does he learn that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב — that it is eaten for two days and one night, from where does he know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the mirror-image question, this time to רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב also agrees that a בכור is eaten for two days and one night. But he used the verse for the birth-year rule. So he needs another source for the eating limit.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it?

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב, נֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד,
phrases.english: And Rav — that it is eaten for two days and one night,
from where does he derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב, נֶאֱכָל לִשְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד, מְנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks רב the mirror-image of the question that was asked of דבי רב in step 11
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רב's source for the two-days-one-night eating limit

steps.title: רב learns it from the breast and thigh of peace offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב learns it from a היקש: the Torah compares the בכור's meat to the חזה ושוק of שלמים. Those are eaten for two days and one night, so the בכור is too.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'And their meat shall be yours, like the breast of waving and like the right thigh.' The verse compared it to the breast and thigh of שלמים. Just as there it is two days and one night, so too here it is two days and one night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב learns the eating limit by comparing the בכור to שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse about the בכור says its meat is 'like the חזה and the שוק.' Those are the כהן's portions of a שלמים, and שלמים may be eaten for two days and one night. Because the Torah put them side by side, the בכור gets the same time limit.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison the Torah makes by placing two things together, so they share laws
The breast and thigh — the כהן's portions of a שלמים
Peace offerings
Just as there, so too here

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree on both laws. They only disagree about which source teaches which: for רב, 'שנה בשנה' gives the birth-year rule and the היקש to שלמים gives the eating limit. For דבי רב, 'שנה בשנה' gives the eating limit and 'כבש בן שנתו' gives the birth-year rule.

phrases.english: He derives it from 'And their meat shall be yours,'
'like the breast of waving and like the right thigh' —
the verse compared it
to the breast and thigh of a peace offering:

phrases.aramaic: מָה לְהַלָּן שְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד,
phrases.english: just as there it is two days and one night,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כָּאן שְׁנֵי יָמִים וְלַיְלָה אֶחָד.
phrases.english: so too here it is two days and one night.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵ״וּבְשָׂרָם יִהְיֶה לָּךְ כַּחֲזֵה הַתְּנוּפָה וּכְשׁוֹק הַיָּמִין״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש compares the בכור to the חזה ושוק of שלמים, which are eaten for two days and one night
